name: Trabectedin (single-agent) for Soft Tissue Sarcoma
cyclesNote: continue to progression or unacceptable toxicity; highest activity in leiomyosarcoma and myxoid/round-cell liposarcoma after an anthracycline. Physician determines duration.

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Soft Tissue Sarcoma (general reference)

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Trabectedin is a histology-directed later-line agent for liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma after anthracycline; myxoid/round-cell liposarcoma (FUS-DDIT3) is notably sensitive. Not molecularly biomarker-restricted for use.

histology: liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma (L-sarcomas) after prior anthracycline

premedications.name: Dexamethasone
premedications.notes: corticosteroid before each infusion for hepatoprotection and antiemesis (e.g. dexamethasone about 20 mg IV before trabectedin). Administer through a central venous line.

supportiveCare: central venous access required for the 24-hour infusion.
monitor liver enzymes and creatine phosphokinase (rhabdomyolysis risk); hold for significant hepatic transaminase elevation or CPK rise.
CBC before each cycle; neutropenia is common.
monitoring: liver function (transaminases, bilirubin) before each cycle

doseModificationRules.condition: transaminase elevation, hyperbilirubinemia, or CPK rise
doseModificationRules.text: Hold until recovery then resume at a reduced dose; discontinue for recurrent grade 3 to 4 hepatic toxicity or rhabdomyolysis. Physician decides.

drugs.name: Trabectedin
drugs.notes: Trabectedin 1.5 mg/m2 IV as a continuous infusion over 24 hours on day 1 every 21 days, through a central venous catheter, with dexamethasone pre-medication. Standard single-agent dosing for L-sarcomas after anthracycline. Dose per the engine from patient BSA. General reference (NCCN / DeVita); own wording, DRAFT.
